clue.text: Bettering the baker by almost 50%, being a livestock auctioneer, say?

definitions.text: Bettering the baker by almost 50%, being a livestock auctioneer, say?

parts.words: Bettering the baker by almost 50%, being a livestock auctioneer, say?
parts.note: an auctioneer gabbles at great speed, so the clue describes the idiom for rapid chatter

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about outdoing a baker while selling cattle at market.
explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen; nineteen beats it by about 46%, so 'nineteen to the dozen' is the baker bettered. Livestock auctioneers are famous for their rapid-fire patter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means chattering very fast without pause, which is exactly how an auctioneer calls bids.

clue.text: Spiritualist Miles knocked out by tense routine

indicators.note: one letter is knocked out of the word and replaced by the letter that does the knocking

parts.note: a medium is a spiritualist who contacts the dead
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A psychic named Miles is undone by the stress of daily routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles' reads as the spiritualist's first name, but it is M, swapped out of MEDIUM for T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is wearisome monotony, the dull sameness of a routine.

clue.text: Fat protecting a grizzly's heart monitor?

indicators.note: the fat wraps around and shields the inner letters, so it is the outer piece of a container

parts.note: lard is rendered pig fat

indicators.note: the heart of the phrase is its central two letters, read across both words

explanation.surface: Fat keeping a grizzly bear's heart safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' takes the middle of the eight-letter phrase 'a grizzly', not of 'grizzly' alone. 'Monitor' looks like a screen or watcher, but it is the reptile, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A monitor is a large tropical reptile, one particular kind of the scaly creature, so it is given by example.

clue.text: Sky region broadcast poison at this point

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters of the word poison are strewn into a new order

parts.note: here means at this point or place

explanation.surface: A news report about poison being spread through the sky right here.
explanation.definitionFit: The ionosphere is a layer of the upper atmosphere, so a region of the sky.

clue.text: Author's description of erotic dancer, live

parts.note: a go-go dancer is a nightclub dancer in revealing costume
L stands for live, as on an electrical terminal

explanation.surface: A writer's account of an erotic dancer performing live.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the author is GO-GO plus L. L is the live wire on a British plug.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikolai Gogol was the Russian writer of Dead Souls and The Overcoat.

clue.text: Stressed, Red backed out, yet to show signs of ageing

definitions.text: yet to show signs of ageing

indicators.note: out says the letters are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: a word that is underlined is stressed or emphasised

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front, so the colour word is written right to left

parts.note: taken as written, the colour

explanation.surface: A stressed communist retreated from politics but still looks youthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns RED into DER, and 'out' takes DER from UNDERLINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin free of lines or wrinkles has not yet begun to show its age.

clue.text: Five earth-filled urinals, recycling all-inclusive

indicators.note: something filled has another piece put within it, so the earth and five go inside
recycling remakes material into new shapes, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
E is the abbreviation for earth, as in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Five muddy urinals being recycled, everything included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycling' rearranges URINALS into UNIRSAL; 'filled' puts VE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something universal applies to every case or person, so it includes all.

clue.text: Dumb, so no good at Scrabble?

definitions.meaning: a Scrabble player who cannot find any words to form would be in this state

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means unable to speak, and taken literally describes having no words to play.

clue.text: See 1 across
Act (before alternative job), making a bit of an entrance

parts.note: do means act or perform
or introduces an alternative
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Performing before taking another job, making an entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorpost is the upright frame at the side of a doorway, part of an entrance.

clue.text: See 1
As a violinist might perform improvised signals at party

indicators.note: something improvised is made up on the spot, so these letters are freshly arranged

parts.note: do is a party; 'at' just places the item

explanation.surface: Musicians make up signals at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvised' gives GLISSAN. 'As a violinist might perform' is fair as glissando is also used adverbially in scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a slide between notes, a technique a violinist uses by gliding a finger along the string.

clue.text: Not looking embarrassed about what you hope to do to this up in the air

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: someone not blushing is un-red

parts.words: what you hope to do to this
parts.note: the solver hopes to solve this crossword

explanation.surface: A confident solver unsure whether this puzzle will get finished.
explanation.walkthrough: UNRED is a made-up word for 'not blushing'; 'this' refers to the crossword itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in the air is an idiom for undecided, a matter still awaiting a settlement.

clue.text: See 24
Sign of letter dropped in the post, or a dodgy "p" for "t"

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shifty, so the letters are rearranged
one letter stands in for another, swapping it out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as the letter T
taken as the letter P

explanation.surface: A letter goes missing in the mail, or a printer slips a p in for a t.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps one T in THE POST for P, and 'dodgy' then rearranges THEPOSP plus ORA.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is the mark showing where letters have been omitted, as in can't.

clue.text: Crushing shame — not lead — poisons us

indicators.note: crushing breaks things into pieces, so the letters are rearranged
the lead of a word is its first letter, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A crushing disgrace poisons our reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not lead' removes the S from SHAME to give HAME; 'Crushing' rearranges HAME plus POISONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans are the species called by the Latin for wise man, so it names ourselves.

clue.text: Having no rival, so unable to strike

definitions.meaning: without a match to strike, so unable to light a fire

explanation.definitionFit: The word means peerless and, read literally, without any matches.

clue.text: Old record kept by courts about Moore, say

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the record sits within the other letters
about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record, an old format

explanation.surface: An old record held in court concerning a Mr Moore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives SCUTOR, and 'kept by' places the record inside it. Henry Moore was a famous British artist working in bronze and stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Moore was an English artist renowned for large bronze figures, so he is an example.

clue.text: See 6
A place for singers, when displaced, to crash — Lil's

indicators.note: displaced means moved out of position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: A choir member is evicted and has to stay at Lil's place.
explanation.definitionFit: Choir stalls are the seats in a church chancel where the choir sits.

clue.text: Crisp, gruesome plot ending as basis for a film?

indicators.note: gruesome suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged
the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A crisp, gory thriller plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gruesome' rearranges CRISP to SCRIP; 'plot ending' adds T.
explanation.definitionFit: A script is the written screenplay from which a film is made.

clue.text: Skilfully dumping a heavyweight writer

indicators.note: dumping means getting rid of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: ably means skilfully
a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight writer cleverly dumped.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid Blyton was the English children's author of the Famous Five books.

clue.text: Many blades needed in the making of this material

definitions.text: Many blades needed in the making of this
definitions.meaning: a stretch of mown grass consists of countless blades
a fine sheer linen or cotton cloth

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a grassed area and a fine cotton or linen fabric.

clue.text: Declamatory Charlie about to snare a party follower (not an unknown)

indicators.note: snaring traps something inside, so the follower goes within the other letters
about suggests turning around, so the letters of the name are rearranged
Y is an algebraic unknown, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a Tory follows the Conservative party

explanation.surface: A ranting Charlie sets out to trap a political supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives RHEICAL, and 'to snare' puts the shortened follower inside. 'Charlie' looks like a person (or slang for a fool) but is just fodder; Y is a standard algebraic unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetorical language is grand and showy, intended to impress, as declamation is.

clue.text: See 1 across
Dot's loaded — flipping piles of money

parts.note: loaded means full

indicators.note: flipping turns the word over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: pots of money means plenty

explanation.surface: Dot is rich, with flipping piles of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. 'flipping' turns POTS into STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is the punctuation dot ending a sentence.

clue.text: Unstable blue rocks in wind start to totter

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other word

parts.note: to wind is to turn

indicators.note: rocks means shakes, so the letters are jumbled
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Unstable blue rocks tremble in the wind before beginning to topple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' gives BULE, placed by 'in'. 'Wind' reads as breeze, but it is the verb, as in winding a handle round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent means agitated and unsettled, lacking steadiness.

clue.text: Spike's bluff

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sharp tip and also a headland projecting into the sea.

clue.text: Breaks (having crushed unionist line) ties?

indicators.note: the breaks squeeze the other letters inside themselves

parts.note: rests are breaks

explanation.surface: Breaks in which a unionist line is crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties are matches in a cup competition, and their outcomes are scores, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Team tennis star performing

parts.note: Chris Evert was a champion tennis player
on means performing, as on stage

explanation.surface: A team tennis star is playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is an English Premier League football club, a sporting side.
